item.title: From anxiety to calm: Chinese support transforms maternal, child healthcare in western Pakistan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 08:49:00
This file photo shows medical supplies donated by China at a hospital in Quetta, Pakistan. (Xinhua) For 28-year-old Gul Bano, the birth of her fourth child brought something she had not experienced during her previous three deliveries -- a sense of calm. Two months ago, Bano arrived at a basic health unit in the provincial capital city of Balochistan to give birth. Unlike her earlier experiences, she found herself surrounded by modern medical equipment, trained health workers, and a clean, well-equipped delivery room. "This time, I was not afraid," Bano said, recalling the day her baby was born. "Everything was available here, and the delivery was much easier than it was a few years ago." Among the equipment that assisted her was a vein detector, which makes it easier to locate veins, particularly when an intravenous line or blood sample is needed, as well as a vacuum extractor, making it easier for her to deliver. For Bano, however, the difference was not only about medical equipment. She said the care she received made her feel respected and comfortable. "My husband works as a daily-wage laborer and earns less than 5 U.S. dollars a day, hindering us as a family from affording quality healthcare. Here, everything was provided to me free of charge, even the delivery gown. The bed was clean, and the equipment was ready," she said. "I did not have to worry about anything." Her experience reflects the changes taking place in maternal and child healthcare facilities across Balochistan. Supported by the government of China, these facilities are offering safer and more dignified childbirth services for mothers. China has been helping the government of Balochistan in upgrading maternal and child healthcare facilities, including the improvement of 100 medical facilities across the province. The cooperation aims to strengthen medical infrastructure, provide modern equipment, and improve services for mothers and newborns, particularly in areas where access to quality healthcare has traditionally been difficult. For women like Bano, these improvements are not simply about new machines or renovated rooms, but can mean the difference between approaching childbirth with anxiety and facing it with confidence. "I am very happy with the treatment I received," she said. "I thank China for helping us. My fourth child arrived not only as a new member of the family, but also as a reminder of how better healthcare can change a mother's experience at one of the most important moments of her life." Balochistan has the highest maternal and neonatal mortality rates in Pakistan, largely because 70 percent of the population lives in remote, scattered and hard-to-reach areas, Sana Furqan, a medical practitioner at the Basic Health Unit in the Hudda locality of Quetta, told Xinhua. "For decades, access has been the biggest barrier. This China-supported project is the first large-scale targeted intervention focused entirely on mothers and children at the primary healthcare level, bringing life-saving care to the doorstep of women in remote districts," she said. Talking about the newly equipped healthcare facilities and renovation, Furqan said the Chinese government has supplied equipment like ultrasound machines, delivery beds, baby warmers, incubators, and essential laboratory equipment. "This upgrade is going to bring proximity, preparedness, timeliness and continuity, which is critical to prevent deaths from postpartum hemorrhage, sepsis and birth asphyxia," she said, adding that it will also provide solar solutions, ambulances, as well as training for female staff. "The project would have transformative impacts on the basic healthcare system of Balochistan. In the medium term, we expect a measurable reduction in maternal mortality ratio and neonatal mortality rate, and a sharp decline in preventable complications," she added. Furqan believes the assistance is not seen as charity, but as brotherhood. "The people of Balochistan, especially its mothers, will never forget that when they needed help the most, China stood with them." In a conversation with Xinhua, Provincial Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said that Pakistan-China cooperation in the health sector is opening a new chapter in people-centered development, turning the friendship between the two countries into tangible benefits for communities. China has one of the most advanced, efficient, and equitable healthcare systems in the world, Kakar said, underlining that despite its own vast population, the country has achieved universal maternal and child health coverage, which is an inspiration for Pakistan. "We want to learn from China's experience in maternal health monitoring, village doctor system, and digital health records," the health minister said.

item.title: Thai medical student finds a calling in acupuncture
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 08:46:00
Salocha Techawanwanitchakorn (R) performs acupuncture on a patient under the guidance of her mentor at the First Teaching Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) in Tianjin, north China, Sept. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Runzhi) A Thai intern gently slid a fine silver needle into an acupoint on a hemiplegic patient's leg. She lifted, thrust and twirled it -- and the motionless leg twitched. Salocha Techawanwanitchakorn, an intern at the First Teaching Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) in north China, had just felt what she came to China to learn. "At that moment," she said, "I knew I had made the right choice to study TCM." Techawanwanitchakorn grew up around the herbal shops of Bangkok's Chinatown, where the air was thick with the scent of Chinese medicine. Her Chinese grandmother was a regular there, buying herbs, and the family relied on TCM to stay healthy. As a child, Techawanwanitchakorn saw TCM as little more than bitter brews and needles. She didn't understand it, but a seed had already been planted. Later, Techawanwanitchakorn came to Tianjin for high school. A class visit to the First Teaching Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine gave her a first close look at TCM. "I was struck," she said. "TCM doesn't just ease symptoms. It treats the root cause." That visit convinced her to study TCM there, and later she entered Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine. Getting to grips with TCM was not easy. In her first year, concepts like meridians and "qi," or vital energy -- invisible and intangible -- left Techawanwanitchakorn baffled. Classical texts full of traditional characters read like a book from another world. None of it deterred the Thai student, however. The following year, Techawanwanitchakorn began studying acupuncture, practicing on herself first. "I felt soreness, numbness, distension and an electric-like tingle at acupoints on my own limbs," she said. "Only then did I know how to put a patient at ease." "Even if a patient's symptoms improve by half, I'm happy," said Techawanwanitchakorn, who specializes in acupuncture as a graduate student. During her clinical internship, Techawanwanitchakorn kept a notebook in her white coat pocket, filled with Chinese and Thai notes on acupoints, prescriptions and the key points her teachers stressed. She came to understand that needling is not just about finding the right acupoint, but about feeling the needle sensation under her hand. Since patients differ in build, the angle and depth of insertion must be adjusted accordingly. The longer she studied under her Chinese teachers, the more she realized that hands-on skill was only the first step. "A good doctor sees not only the disease but also the person," her mentor told her. At first, patients took her accent as a sign that she was from southern China. When they learned she was Thai, some greeted her with "Sawasdee kha (hello)," and said "Khob khun kha (thank you)" after she removed the needles. Others said she was the best foreign student at needling they had ever seen. "Experience is built needle by needle," Techawanwanitchakorn said. In clinical practice, Techawanwanitchakorn has seen more and more patients recover through acupuncture, and has come to appreciate TCM's unique strength in treating the whole patient. Her resolve to study TCM has only grown firmer. TCM, she believes, remains full of vitality after being passed down for thousands of years. In Thailand, too, many hospitals have TCM departments, and more young Thais are willing to try it. Techawanwanitchakorn, being one of them, has brought TCM home. Last summer, back in Thailand, she administered acupuncture to her sister, who had back pain. Though afraid of needles at first, her sister later said she felt "much more relaxed." Techawanwanitchakorn also used cupping equipment brought from China to treat her mother. In her daily life, she has adopted TCM-inspired habits, drinking chrysanthemum tea and paying more attention to her routine. The student is now interning while preparing for China's physician licensing exam. She hopes to stay in China first to gain clinical experience, then return to Thailand to promote TCM. "China has more patients and more complex cases, so there is more to learn," she said. "I will bring what I learned in China back to Thailand and let more people see the charm of TCM."

item.title: China's Blue Bay Restoration Initiative named UN World Restoration Flagship
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 08:13:00
China's Blue Bay Restoration Initiative is named a World Restoration Flagship by the United Nations during the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia, Oct. 29, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Junfeng) China's Blue Bay Restoration Initiative was named a World Restoration Flagship by the United Nations on Thursday during the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia. The initiative is jointly led by China's Ministry of Natural Resources and Ministry of Finance. This marks the second time a nationwide ecological restoration initiative from China has received the United Nations Decade on Ecosystem Restoration recognition, making China the first country to achieve the distinction twice. Chosen from over 200 applications and more than 80 government-submitted nominations, the Blue Bay Restoration Initiative was recognized as one of the world's most promising, ambitious and inspiring examples of large-scale ecosystem restoration, said Inger Andersen, executive director of the UN Environment Programme. The initiative aims to restore more than 150,000 hectares of coastal wetlands and over 2,000 km of coastline by 2030, bringing lasting benefits to local communities, she added.

item.title: Smart, green and service-oriented: Canton Fair mirrors new momentum in China's foreign trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 08:12:00
A staff member controls a smart wheelchair to go down the stairs during the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) The 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, is showcasing smart, green and service-oriented products, with high-tech, customized and low-carbon debuts drawing global buyers and highlighting new opportunities for Chinese manufacturing. Logistics robots, drink-making robots and pet-companion robots crowded the intelligent robotics area at the fair, which is being held from Oct. 15 to Nov. 4 in Guangzhou, capital of south China's Guangdong Province. At the booth of Hangzhou Taixi Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., buyers lined up to try out a consumer waist-assist exoskeleton. Many overseas buyers held the handrail and shuffled forward, step by step, to feel how the device relieves pressure on their lower limbs. It is the first flagship product to integrate its human-oriented physical AI technology roadmap, said company founder Liang Linchao. The device uses waist motors and sensors to detect movement and assist lower-limb mobility. Its weight has been cut to about 2 kg, and alongside a refined appearance, algorithms and gait plans tailored to elderly people and hemiplegic patients have been added. The cluster of cutting-edge smart equipment reflects a broader push toward industrial innovation. At this fair, 64 percent of exhibitors have integrated the industrial internet and artificial intelligence into R&D and production, and new products accounted for 23.2 percent of exhibits, marking a record high. "At today's Canton Fair, consumer electronics are the dominant category, and tech products such as new energy storage, embodied intelligence and smart healthcare are eye-catching, with many cutting-edge Chinese-made products making their debut," said Zhang Li, an official with the Ministry of Commerce. A robot demonstrates stair climbing skills at the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) Nearby, several European buyers closely watched the scrolling data at DSL Tech Group's booth. The AI-POOL low-chlorine intelligent pool system uses sensor probes to collect the pool's real-time indicators such as residual chlorine, pH level, turbidity and water pressure, and automatically coordinates pumps, disinfection units and sand-filter backwash systems. Chen Meixiang, the representative of the company, demonstrated on her phone how users can receive alerts about water quality abnormalities from thousands of miles away. The system adjusts automatically, so staff no longer need to visit regularly to take samples and mix chemicals. "Many overseas private pools used to rely on maintenance workers visiting once a week, and water quality would easily exceed standards," Chen said. These European clients are mainly pool operation and maintenance service providers, attracted by the system's ability to cut manual maintenance costs. These technology-driven products are also reflected in trade data. Customs statistics show that in the first three quarters of 2026, China's total imports and exports of industrial robots, electronic components, computer parts and electrical equipment exceeded 10 trillion yuan (1.49 trillion U.S. dollars), up 58.9 percent year on year, driving overall import and export growth by 11.3 percentage points. Liu Chun, president of the China Chamber of Commerce for Import and Export of Machinery and Electronic Products, said that driven by technological innovation and industrial upgrading, high-tech and high-value-added products are gradually becoming the main growth engine of foreign trade, pushing "China's smart manufacturing" toward the high end of global industrial and value chains. This service-oriented approach is visible at the booth of Shandong Linuo Paradigma Co., Ltd., where sales staff explained tailored plans to buyers from different continents. Overseas buyers view a solar panel cleaner during the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Lu Hanxin) "Africa lacks power and is windy and dusty, so we cut costs and provide solar water-heating systems that are easy to install and run without electricity," a staff member of the company said. "The Middle East wants high quality, so we match energy-saving products with high-standard certification, and South Asia emphasizes large capacity and durability, so we strengthen system adaptability." The company has set up agent systems and localized service outlets in markets of Belt and Road partner countries, combining Chinese manufacturing, German-partnered technology and global service into a competitive edge. Beyond individual products, the latest edition of the Canton Fair also features a batch of prefabricated new products, including space capsules, portable integrated kitchens and modular homestay houses. Chinese suppliers are moving from selling parts to selling whole houses, and integrated overseas expansion is supporting a new growth path. "By launching prefabricated building solutions for cultural tourism camps, we have attracted buyers from Australia, Brazil, and Saudi Arabia among other countries, and more than 300 have reached preliminary agreements. We will continue to use project meetings to deliver full-chain services from planning to design, construction and operation," said Jia Xuehong, planning and design director of Chongqing SUNDON Prefabricated Construction and Technology Co., Ltd. More and more foreign trade companies are shifting from simply taking orders and shipping goods to building systems and exporting supporting services. At the fair, 36.5 percent of exhibitors have started a transformation of "product plus service." For the first time, the trade services zone covers all 10 major categories of producer services, including logistics and warehousing, industrial design, overseas operation and maintenance, cross-border investment and financing and other supporting services, building a one-stop support platform for companies expanding overseas. Overseas buyers communicate during the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) Yang Jie, secretary-general of the Guangdong Industrial Design Association, said that under an industrial design and R&D approach that runs through the whole life cycle and centers on consumer pain points, more and more Chinese companies are winning favor in more markets by integrating design into the early stages of development and coordinating it with technology to deliver innovative products and solutions. Green products are another highlight. Amid the global energy transition, green products and low-carbon technologies have become highly sought-after in international markets. At the fair, exhibitor Xiamen HiTHIUM Energy Storage Technology focused on showcasing its flagship long-duration energy storage products, presenting stable and reliable long-duration power supply solutions to overseas buyers. Wang Pengcheng, co-founder and CEO of the company, said more and more countries and regions are advancing energy structure transition, and the company hopes that through the Canton Fair, the "Chinese solution" for long-duration energy storage can be seen by the world, so that more countries have the option of using stable, green and affordable clean power. China is enriching global supply with quality green and smart products and helping accelerate the global green, low-carbon and digital and intelligent transition. Over the past decade, China has provided more than 80 percent of the world's photovoltaic modules and 70 percent of its wind power equipment, effectively driving down the cost of global wind and solar power generation. Commenting on the trend, Liang Yutian, associate dean of the Institute of International and Regional Studies, Sun Yat-sen University, said the concentrated display of new energy, energy storage equipment, green home appliances and other products reflects the global green transition forming new market demand. In the future, around the digital economy, green energy, smart manufacturing and low-carbon technologies, countries can further strengthen technological cooperation, industrial coordination and standards alignment to cultivate new international growth points. From continuous breakthroughs in hard technology to complete solutions stepping into the spotlight, and green thinking embedded in products, the innovation vitality surging at the Canton Fair illustrates how China's foreign trade keeps cultivating new advantages and deepening its links with the world.

item.title: CPC plenum concludes, adopting resolution on persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 23:55:00
Top News The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held its fifth plenary session from Monday to Thursday in Beijing, adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presided over the meeting. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, said a communique issued after the session, per the Xinhua News Agency. According to the communique issued after the session, the meeting adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Chinese experts said the fifth plenary session underscores the CPC's determination to strengthen internal discipline and sustain its anti-corruption campaign, while reinforcing the Party's capacity to govern at a critical stage in China's development. The experts stressed that the greatest threats to a ruling party can come from within, making sustained self-governance and strict internal discipline essential to avoiding the historical cycle of rise and decline. Moreover, as China advances its modernization drive, the session carries broader significance for maintaining policy continuity, strengthening governance and laying the groundwork for the country's long-term development. Rigorous self-governance At the session, the CPC Central Committee gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era. It was pointed out that as the Party endeavors to supervise, govern, develop, and strengthen itself in the new era, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking, and new strategies in response to the major questions of the times -- what kind of long-term governing Marxist party the CPC should build and how to build it, thereby giving rise to Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. "It was stressed that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we also face many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor," the communique said. Profound changes in global, national, and Party conditions have made the CPC's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more formidable, it added. At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted as follows: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations. Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session with the emphasis on strengthening the Party spirit of Communists; strictly practicing democratic centralism; cultivating high-caliber officials capable of shouldering the mission of national rejuvenation; building a well-knit organizational system characterized by cross-level alignment and effective implementation; improving conduct and tightening discipline on an ongoing basis; taking firm and coordinated action against corruption; running the Party with systems and regulations; refining Party and state oversight systems; and ensuring all responsibilities of Party self-supervision and self-governance are fulfilled in earnest, according to the communique. Strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, it noted. Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique, adding that it is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organizations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. Improving conduct and tightening discipline are effective measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. "It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption," the communique said. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," it stated. The purpose of strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance is to make the Communist Party of China (CPC) stronger, Xin Ming, a professor at the School of Marxism, Beihang University, told the Global Times. He noted that the strength comes from continuous self-reform and self-improvement, rooting out problems that undermine the Party's health, so that it can remain vigorous and better fulfill its responsibilities and missions. Advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance is also a process of ensuring that the CPC stays true to its founding mission of serving the people, enabling it to pursue the long-term interests of society rather than catering to particular groups for short-term gains or yielding to external interference, Chen Shu, a professor from the Party School of the CPC Central Committee, told the Global Times. Chen noted that the greatest threats often come from within, stressing that maintaining strict internal discipline is essential to overcoming the historical cycle of rise and decline and ensuring lasting stability. General Secretary Xi has led an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign since 2012, driven by a determination to "offend a few thousand rather than fail 1.4 billion." The campaign has targeted corrupt officials at both high and low levels, according to a Xinhua report. An official review of work in 2025 reported that disciplinary and supervisory bodies nationwide investigated 967,000 cases of misconduct and corruption affecting people's daily lives, returning or helping recover about 77.6 billion yuan ($11.5 billion) in money and property to the public. Far-reaching significance Studying and implementing the guiding principles from this plenary session represent a major political task for the entire Party both at present and in the period to come, according to the communique. It was also stressed that all aspects of the Party's work agenda should be steadily advanced at the turn of the year. The CPC Central Committee decided at the session that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027 and stated that this congress, which is to be held at a critical stage for basically realizing socialist modernization and on a new journey toward the Second Centenary Goal, will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country. The session elected Zhang Shengmin as a new member of the CPC Central Committee Political Bureau, according to the communique. The session also decided on the filling of empty seats on the Central Committee by alternate members, deliberated and adopted inspection reports of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Central Military Commission on those committing grave violations of discipline and laws, and confirmed the Political Bureau's previous decisions to punish those violators. The CPC Central Committee called upon the entire Party to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core and fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. As China enters a critical phase of its modernization drive, the fifth plenary session's emphasis on tightening Party discipline and strengthening internal governance is of particular significance. Achieving the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) requires a particular focus on improving the Party's capacity and competence in steering economic and social development, analysts said. The CPC's capacity to mobilize society and sustain long-term development has rested on its political leadership, policy planning and institutional framework. Strengthening the Party's capacity to govern is crucial to carrying out China's long-term development agenda, Xin noted.

item.title: To understand the new 'Made in China' era, the West must shed prejudices: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 23:26:00
Dozens of UBTECH industrial humanoid robots carry out training tasks at a smart factory in the Qianwan New Area in Ningbo, East China's Zhejiang Province, on March 1, 2025. Photo: VCG The new face of "Made in China" is a transition from advantages of scale to systemic strengths, from cost competitiveness to innovation prowess, and from exporting goods to exporting capabilities. What the West truly needs to update is its entrenched mind-set of viewing China's development as a "zero-sum threat." On Thursday, Reuters published an article titled "Welcome to the new 'Made in China.'" Coining the term "new 'Made in China,'" the piece observed that Chinese manufacturing is expanding from cheap clothing, furniture, and toys into automobiles, complex machinery, high-end chemicals, and data center equipment. However, reading between the lines, the report remains accustomed to attributing China's competitiveness to subsidies, low prices, and "overcapacity." What does the new "Made in China" truly look like? Detaching oneself from an understanding of industrial ecosystems and competitive dynamics easily leads to the fallacy of "the blind men and the elephant" - mistaking a single leg for the entire creature. China's manufacturing sector is increasingly serving as the "factory of factories" supporting global industrial production. The strength of Chinese manufacturing is demonstrated not only in finished consumer products, but even more so in its capacity to provide critical equipment and foundational inputs for global production. Today, from precision control boards and specialized cabling to high-end machine tools and industrial robotics, Chinese manufacturing has become an indispensable component of global industrial upgrading and AI computing infrastructure. In the first three quarters of 2026, equipment manufacturing contributed nearly 90 percent of China's export growth. This vividly confirms a broader transition: China is steadily evolving from a provider of consumer goods into a pivotal supply-side hub for global productive capacity, while the bedrock of its competitiveness has upgraded from single-product price advantages to the systemic operational efficiency of an entire industrial ecosystem. The competitiveness of Chinese manufacturing has forged ahead through thorough market competition and continuous innovation. While subsidies may influence short-term costs, they can never replace a firm's long-term accumulation built through the process of market trial and error, process refinement, and rapid responsiveness to demand. Supported by an ultra-large domestic market, full-chain industrial integration, and a vast pool of engineering talent, new technologies in China swiftly transition from laboratory concepts to mass production before diffusing into adjacent sectors. Manufacturing competition itself has escalated into a contest of cross-industry technology transfer: perception and localization technologies developed for new-energy vehicles are spilling over into smart equipment, while the consumer robotics sector has pivoted from price wars toward competition over quality and brand reputation. Overseas consumer perceptions of Chinese products are similarly shifting - from "low price" to "technologically advanced and reliable." Brand premiums are increasingly determined by the speed of innovation and user acclaim. Dismissing the growth of Chinese manufacturing simply with terms like "subsidies" and "dumping" is not only factually incorrect, but also misreads the trajectory of global industry. Chinese manufacturing is evolving from exporting individual products to delivering comprehensive solutions. Research and development, design, manufacturing, digital operations and maintenance, and after-sales services are becoming deeply integrated. Industrial equipment manufacturers now provide customers with remote monitoring, preventive maintenance, and full lifecycle management, while logistics equipment companies integrate forklifts, warehousing systems, and digital platforms to improve customers' overall production efficiency. What Chinese companies deliver is no longer just individual pieces of hardware, but also the operation of entire production lines and support for complete production systems. The focus of value creation is consequently shifting toward system integration and long-term services. Meanwhile, China continues to advance institutional opening-up, making it clear that goods manufactured in China that meet domestic product standards are eligible for relevant government procurement support policies on an equal basis, regardless of whether their producers are domestic or foreign-invested enterprises. This latest round of upgrading is also opening up broader opportunities for global companies to participate in the Chinese market and leverage China's comprehensive industrial ecosystem. Trade barriers cannot override the economic forces that underpin industrial competitiveness. Tariffs may alter trade routes, but they cannot conjure up mature supply chains, a well-established pool of engineering talent, or deeply integrated industrial capabilities. Erecting barriers against Chinese intermediate goods and production equipment would instead raise the overall costs of industrial investment and technological upgrading in the countries imposing them. For countries determined to revitalize domestic manufacturing, shutting out cost-effective production inputs would not only fail to deliver the intended benefits but could also undermine the competitiveness of their domestic companies in third-country markets. The new face of "Made in China" is a transition from advantages of scale to systemic strengths, from cost competitiveness to innovation prowess, and from exporting goods to exporting capabilities. Every country has the right to develop its manufacturing sector, and every country has opportunities to participate in the international division of labor and benefit from technological progress. What the West truly needs to update is its entrenched mind-set of viewing China's development as a "zero-sum threat." Only by approaching competition with an open mind can countries create room for cooperation, and only by respecting objective economic laws can they turn the global trend of industrial upgrading into tangible opportunities for mutual benefit and win-win outcomes.

item.title: Humanoid robot firms including AgiBot report rapid revenue growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:31:00
An AgiBot robot gives a tea ceremony demonstration at Chimelong Spaceship Park in Hengqin, Zhuhai, South China's Guangdong Province. Photo: Courtesy of Chimelong Group Multiple Chinese developers of humanoid robots have released upbeat financial and operational figures, showing robust revenue expansion amid the accelerating global adoption of embodied artificial intelligence (AI) machines. Peng Zhihui, co-founder of AgiBot, said on Thursday that the company's revenue for the first half of 2026 came close to 2 billion yuan ($300 million). The firm disclosed that the cumulative production of its general-purpose AI humanoid robots had hit 20,000 units as of September. In comparison, AgiBot achieved revenue of 1.05 billion yuan for the full year of 2025, it revealed in April this year. In terms of shipments, AgiBot said that it shipped 9,700 humanoid robots in the first half of 2026, capturing a 43.1 percent global market share and retaining its top spot worldwide, citing data from Counterpoint Research. "These figures demonstrate our capacity to manufacture robots in a sustained, stable and large-scale manner — and crucially, to deploy them effectively. Building a functional prototype in a lab, designing a product fit for mass production, and establishing supply chains, quality control systems, production rhythms, delivery networks and long-term maintenance frameworks are entirely separate challenges," the company told the Global Times on Thursday. Peer rival Unitree Robotics also delivered strong results. Its revenue reached 1.817 billion yuan in the first nine months, up 55.71 percent year-on-year, while net profit attributable to shareholders surged 270.54 percent to 387 million yuan, according to the company's financial report. Third-quarter revenue rose 69.93 percent to 665 million yuan. Siasun Robot & Automation released its third-quarter results on Wednesday, showing that the industrial robot giant generated 986 million yuan in revenue, up 76.6 percent year-on-year. The humanoid robot sector is at a critical takeoff stage, transitioning from technical validation toward large-scale real-world deployment. Leading players have generally posted rapid revenue growth, fueled by unlocked mass-production capabilities, expanding domestic use cases and rising overseas sales, Wang Peng, an associate research fellow at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times on Thursday. The growth logic of the industry has shifted from its early reliance on demonstration orders and policy-backed pilot projects to sustained penetration into genuine commercial scenarios. Regular deployments are gaining greater traction across the industrial, cultural tourism, research and education sectors, he added. The industry is undergoing supply-side consolidation and upgrades of its business model. Top firms are moving beyond pure hardware sales toward integrated solutions with long-term operational services. Aligned with the push for new quality productive forces, the industry is rapidly building a globally competitive Chinese robotics ecosystem, Wang noted. China is now home to more than 140 humanoid robot manufacturers. In 2025, producers shipped 14,400 humanoid robots, accounting for roughly eight in every 10 units shipped globally, the Xinhua News Agency reported in September. Market watchers said that the strong revenue numbers represent a milestone for China's humanoid robot sector, proving that local industrial chains are capable of supporting mass manufacturing, rather than merely building prototype units. But industry insiders cautioned that large-scale production is not the finish line of commercialization. Competitions may showcase robots' extreme performance limits, yet real value comes from steady commercial deployment. These robots are designed not only for demonstration events, but also for long-term operation inside factories, shopping malls and other real-world sites, they said.

item.title: Why ASEAN won't buy Australian defence chief's claims on Chinese military
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:16:00
Australia's Defence Minister Richard Marles arrives before the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus in Cebu, Philippines, on October 29, 2026. Photo: VCG During the 20th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting in Manila, Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles once again trotted out the same old script: making unsubstantiated claims about "China's military buildup" and trying to use that as a pretext to push for closer ties among the so-called Squad - a small circle comprising the US, Japan, the Philippines and Australia. What Marles is essentially claiming boils down to this: China's defence development amounts to "applying pressure," while Australia's own military build-up is about "upholding the rules." These are blatant double standards. The regional "pressure" narrative reads more like a tailor‑made talking point for exclusive defence cliques. Yu Lei, a professor at the School of Northeast Asian Studies, Shandong University, noted that by making up claims about China's military, Marles is trying to force Southeast Asian nations to take sides. This seeks to erode the ASEAN-centric multilateral security architecture, replace Southeast Asia's open and inclusive regional order with bloc-driven confrontation and secure legitimacy for Australia's own military buildup. Yu further pointed out that Southeast Asian countries pursue an open, inclusive ASEAN-centered order and stand for safeguarding their autonomy and national interests through multilateral consultations. "The approach of making up threats while pushing for small military blocs will not only fail to win the support of Southeast Asia, but will also undermine Australia's sovereignty, interests and regional credibility." In fact, China has consistently adhered to the principles of amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness in its neighborhood diplomacy. It emphasizes the need to base its actions on the United Nations Charter and international law, opposes the instrumentalization and bloc-based use of "rules," and advocates building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future through dialogue and cooperation, rather than "suppressing" other countries' legitimate rights to development through security alliances. China's defense spending accounts for less than 1.5 percent of its GDP. It is significantly lower than that of major military powers like the US, and is also below the global average. In contrast, Australia is vigorously advancing the AUKUS nuclear submarine program, investing tens of billions of Australian dollars to procure nuclear-powered submarines and long-range strike capabilities, expanding military bases in the north, and frequently conducting joint exercises with extra-regional forces in the South China Sea and waters surrounding the Philippines. It's clear who is putting pressure on regional peace and stability. What truly brings uncertainty to these waters are the frequent close-proximity activities of non-regional naval vessels and aircraft, as well as exclusionary defense arrangements intended for confrontation. Southeast Asian nations can clearly see who has been flip-flopping on the South China Sea issue, who is building bridges and roads in the Mekong subregion, who fuels militarization, who pushes for an exclusive restructuring of the regional security architecture, and who is committed to open and inclusive regional cooperation. For more than 30 years since China and ASEAN established their dialogue relationship, China has consistently participated in regional affairs with a constructive attitude, which in itself is the most concrete interpretation of "rules." Since 2020, China and ASEAN have consistently been each other's largest trading partners, and landmark projects such as the China-Laos Railway have delivered tangible benefits to local people. By contrast, security arrangements involving Australia often leave Southeast Asia with nothing but the roar of military exercises and the burden of defense spending. If Marles truly cares about the region, he should respect the right of countries to independently choose their own security paths, rather than trying to tell them what to do. In fact, it is clear Marles' rhetoric does not reflect any genuine concern for regional security, but rather anxiety over his own problematic defense agenda. It is becoming increasingly difficult to justify the hundreds of billions of Australian dollars invested in AUKUS nuclear submarines to the Australian people. Manufacturing claims about threats won't help with that.

item.title: GT Voice: SK shipbuilding's high-end edge hinges on Asian industrial collaboration
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:12:00
Visitors check out ship models at a booth during the Offshore Korea 2026 held in Busan, South Korea on October 14, 2026. Photo: VCG South Korea's shipbuilders posted third-quarter profits driven by high value vessels; however, sustaining their high end edge calls for regional industrial collaboration rather than yielding to external geopolitical demands that risk eroding long term industrial strengths. HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering announced on Wednesday that its third-quarter operating profit rose 37.3 percent year-on-year, driven by higher ship prices and strong earnings from its engine and offshore businesses, The Korea Herald reported. This strong performance is far from an isolated case. South Korea's three major shipbuilders all achieved relatively robust results in the third quarter of this year. Samsung Heavy Industries announced that its operating profit for the quarter increased by 42 percent year-on-year, bringing the combined operating profit of the three shipbuilders to 2.27 trillion won ($1.7 billion). This growth is attributed to continued revenue from high-value-added vessels, such as liquefied natural gas carriers. Behind these numbers lies the payoff of South Korea's shipbuilding sector in terms of high-value ship segments, a clear sign that it retains formidable competitiveness in premium shipbuilding markets. Yet the realization of the high-end ship dividend does not mean that competition will ease. High profitability tends to attract more resources into the high-end market. Global new ship orderbooks have seen China's share steadily rise amid intensifying market competition. If South Korea relies solely on the brand and technological reputation it has built up while neglecting supply-chain efficiency and sustained research and development, its high-end edge could be gradually squeezed. Holding the leading position requires more than winning high-priced orders; it demands stable delivery, consolidation of core supporting industries, cultivation of technical talent, and the continuous creation of new product advantages. This is precisely why South Korea's shipbuilding sector needs stable regional industrial collaboration more than ever. After decades of growth, Asia's shipbuilding industrial chain has formed a close, sophisticated division of labor that cannot be easily severed. The interconnected ecosystem spans parts supply, materials and equipment, vessel design technology, and specialized skilled personnel. Even as companies across the region compete fiercely for new orders, they can still identify shared interests in supply chain coordination, technical exchanges, and alignment of industry standards. To channel all their resources into technological upgrades and consolidate their hold on high-end segments, South Korea's shipbuilders need the support of the Asian industrial ecosystem. The coexistence of competition and cooperation has become a reality for Asia's shipbuilding landscape. Any attempt to break these deeply integrated industrial ties will ultimately undermine South Korea's own core competitiveness. At this critical juncture, persistent efforts by the US to poach South Korean shipbuilding capacity and pull it into its own industrial arrangements deserve particular vigilance. Such "cooperation" may appear to bring new orders and market access, but if its essence is to steer South Korean firms to channel their capital, technology, talent, and key production capacity toward serving America's industrial goals, South Korea must carefully assess the long-term costs. Shipbuilding is not a single factory that can be relocated at will. Its competitiveness is built on decades of accumulated supplier networks, engineering expertise, and seamless industrial collaboration. Restructuring production outside this established system will not only drive up costs across supply chains, personnel training, and operational coordination, but also divert resources that should be dedicated to South Korea's own industrial upgrading, potentially allowing its clearly laid-out development roadmap to be hijacked by external strategic priorities. Whether South Korea's shipbuilding sector can hold onto today's achievements will depend entirely on its willingness to keep innovating amid intensifying competition and seizing the initiative while deepening mutually beneficial regional cooperation. By expanding pragmatic regional collaboration, South Korea can turn its current profit into a solid foundation for long-term growth. Advancing regional cooperation is a key way for South Korea to translate today's profits into a foundation for lasting growth, rather than gradually consuming the industrial advantages in the course of catering to external geopolitical demands.

item.title: Restoring lakes and surrounding landscapes helps strengthen northern China's ecological security barrier
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 21:52:00
Migratory birds fly over the shores of Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, in March 2026. Photo: Courtesy of Ulanqab Publicity Department Waterbirds floated on Daihai Lake, lowered their heads to feed and occasionally took wing across its surface. Even in late October, as the weather grew colder, the lake in Liangcheng county, Ulanqab, North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, remained a feeding and resting place for birds. "Many birds have already flown south," Yu Lei, deputy director of the county's Daihai Nature Reserve Service Center in Ulanqab, told the Global Times, pointing toward the water. Earlier this year, the reserve recorded something it had never documented before: oriental storks nesting and breeding locally. Two nests on high-voltage pylons produced six chicks, adding a breeding record for a nationally protected species to the lake's changing ecological history. The conditions supporting those nests have required work far beyond the shoreline. Around Ulanqab's lakes, restoration has extended into surrounding farmland, industrial facilities and neighboring regions, connecting wildlife protection with changes in how people use land and water. Chinese President Xi Jinping stressed upholding a holistic and systematic approach to the conservation and improvement of mountains, waters, forests, farmlands, grasslands and deserts. During a recent inspection in Ulanqab, he called for promoting concerted efforts to cut carbon emissions, reduce pollution, expand green development and pursue economic growth, while unswervingly following the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. During a recent visit, the Global Times reporter found that coordinated restoration efforts were helping revive lakes and wetlands, bringing wildlife back and supporting new livelihoods for nearby communities in Ulanqab. A place to breed Yu remembers the details of the storks' first breeding season clearly. Each nest contained four eggs, and three chicks hatched in each. For him, their presence raised a practical question about what the lake could now provide. "Why would oriental storks come here, and even build nests and hatch their young?" he said. "First, there has to be food - there have to be fish in the lake. Then, there has to be safety, without so much disturbance from people, before they will settle here." He recalled a much harsher period around 2016, when fish disappeared from the lake for a time. As the water volume fell, substances in the remaining water became more concentrated and the water quality deteriorated, he explained. Fish have been recorded again since 2023, with additional species appearing in subsequent monitoring. Daihai relies mainly on surrounding rivers and rainfall for replenishment. Local people describe the region's recurring droughts with a saying: "Nine years out of 10 are dry," Yu said. Restoring the lake, therefore, required securing water while reducing the demands placed upon it. One major intervention brought water from the Yellow River. The river is roughly 160 kilometers away, Yu said, and the water must be lifted through three stages of pumping to reach Daihai. The emergency ecological replenishment project began supplying water in September 2022. Conservation measures also reached the surrounding fields. About 260,000 mu, or approximately 17,333 hectares, of farmland underwent conversion from irrigated to dryland farming. Farmers adjusted their crops, replacing water-intensive maize with relatively drought-tolerant sorghum, millet and soybeans, Yu introduced. "Previously, maize might need watering two or three times a year. Switching to these grains can save quite a bit of water," he said. Affected farmers received subsidies to support the adjustment. Industrial water use changed as well. The Daihai power plant shifted from water cooling toward air cooling and began using treated reclaimed water for production, reducing its reliance on lake water and groundwater. Wetland vegetation restoration, village sewage treatment, livestock-pollution control and grazing restrictions addressed other pressures on the lake. Yu now puts the reserve's bird records at 113 species, compared with 68 previously. Great bustards have arrived to overwinter every year since 2020, with about 40 monitored this October. Three red-crowned cranes also spent the winter at Daihai in January 2024. The lake's changing surroundings have also become part of local livelihoods. A local report provided to the Global Times describes Hu Dengyu, a resident of Fujia village, who sold his 200 sheep in 2003 and bought a secondhand sightseeing boat with room for 30 passengers. After replacing his boat over the years, he now operates one with 78 seats. Hu also helps operate a patrol boat for the reserve after the tourist season. Yu said tourism must remain within defined limits. "Visitors cannot go wherever they like. The reserve cannot be entered freely, and tourism activities must take place in designated areas. We cannot damage the environment again by developing tourism." Three staff members take a boat out on Daihai Lake in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, on August 26, 2026. Photo: VCG Following the water At Huangqihai Lake, another Ulanqab wetland, wind moved through the reeds as flocks crossed the sunlit water and settled on nearby shallows. No tourists were in sight, and the sounds of wind and birds could be heard along the shore. In 2025, villagers noticed something in the birds' beaks: fish. The sight suggested that fish were becoming more plentiful in the lake, giving local people and reserve staff another way to recognize ecological change. Wang Shaojun, director of the Huangqihai Lake Nature Reserve Service Center, told the Global Times that, after about 27 years, fish activity was again detected in the lake in 2025. The fish found were mainly crucian carp, alongside smaller numbers of common carp and loaches after a gap of about 27 years. Fishing is now prohibited to protect the resource. The lake had almost dried up in 2006. Even after water returned in 2012, its surface area fluctuated from about 25 square kilometers in wetter periods to less than 5 square kilometers during dry seasons. By the end of September 2026, the water covered 85.22 square kilometers, according to local briefing materials. Reducing disturbance has been a sustained part of the work. Before the reserve was established, people lived, cultivated land, grazed livestock and operated breeding facilities within the area. As protection increased, residents were encouraged to adjust their livelihoods, with some moving into employment or business in nearby towns. Fencing of the core protected area began in 2017. Around it, farmland was taken out of cultivation and returned to wetland, reducing agricultural inputs such as pesticides, fertilizers and plastic film. Environmental improvements in surrounding villages addressed additional sources of pollution. Sixteen livestock farms within the reserve were dismantled or relocated. Their departure reduced both production activity and pollution sources, creating space for the wetland to recover. The lake's connections extend well beyond the reserve boundary. Its basin crosses seven county-level administrative areas, with 11 rivers feeding the closed inland lake. Therefore, upstream vegetation, water withdrawals and pollution affect what reaches the lake basin, the Global Times learned from the local publicity department. Increased rainfall in recent years has also played an important role in replenishing the lake, alongside restoration and water management measures. The lake's expansion reflects both changes in natural conditions and efforts to reduce pressure from human activities. The reserve has recorded 168 bird species. Wang said protecting Huangqihai contributes to the wider task of strengthening northern China's ecological security barrier. For staff watching birds catch fish again, that task has a visible expression on the water. An aerial view of Daihai Lake in Ulanqab, North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region Photo: VCG Protection across boundaries Another breeding scene appeared this summer at Chahan Naoer National Wetland Park in Shangyi county, North China's Hebei Province. Monitoring staff recorded more than 300 floating nests of black-necked grebes near the park's wooden boardwalks, the largest recorded breeding aggregation of the species in Hebei, according to the Hebei Daily. The wetland straddles Hebei and Inner Mongolia, with national wetland parks on the Shangyi and Shangdu sides. Its wider basin crosses nine county-level administrative areas, making coordination part of the everyday work of protection. The two parks signed a cooperation memorandum in 2025. Their arrangements include quarterly coordination meetings, joint monitoring records and public education. By mid-October, they had issued three joint monitoring records, the local publicity department introduced. Staff from Shangyi have also been incorporated into the team of the wetland's national observation and research station. Monitoring coverage has expanded to the Shangyi park, and the two sides use drones to jointly track changes in the water surface. That shared work is helping build a fuller account of the wetland's birds. Third-quarter joint monitoring and data-sharing recorded 202 species in the basin, compared with 79 in 2020. On the Shangdu side, water conservation has included converting 145,300 mu, or about 9,687 hectares, of irrigated farmland to dryland farming and closing 1,551 irrigation wells within the basin. Decisions about vegetation have also taken water availability into account. In rehabilitating degraded woodland, authorities have gradually replaced overmature, water-demanding poplars and willows with native drought-tolerant shrubs such as caragana and wild apricot. The work reaches into village routines. In Guojiacun village, water-saving agriculture and the collection of discarded agricultural film have been incorporated into village rules and a points-based rewards system. Through environmental actions, residents can earn rewards. Scientific surveys elsewhere in Inner Mongolia are expanding knowledge of the region's less conspicuous wildlife and plants. A three-year survey in the Inner Mongolia Helan Mountains National Nature Reserve has identified six new species - two vascular plants, three lichens and one insect - and 568 species newly recorded at different geographical levels. The survey filled gaps in knowledge of groups including lichens and mosses, creating a biological database to support management planning and targeted restoration. These findings document organisms previously insufficiently understood. The pressures on such ecosystems extend beyond China. The Convention on Wetlands' Global Wetland Outlook 2025 estimates that about 22 percent of global wetland area has been lost since 1970. Agricultural expansion, pollution, disrupted water flows and climate change are among the interacting pressures identified in the assessment. The work around Ulanqab's lakes connects those pressures with practical decisions: which crops to grow, where to reduce water withdrawals, how neighboring jurisdictions share monitoring and where human activity should leave wildlife undisturbed. Near the end of the Daihai interview, Yu pointed to an old water-lifting facility in the lake. Built when water was scarce, it had become partly submerged as the water rose. Several waterbirds were perched on it, away from people on the shore. "If we had insisted on taking it down back then, the birds might not have this place to rest," he said. "Working with nature may be the best approach," he added, looking across the lake.
